interface.longDescription:
App Builder helps you go from an app idea to a working app by chat. Answer 5 quick questions about your idea and it prepares a personalized link that opens an online app builder with your app ready to build. It also writes code, plans and copy you can use right away.

What you can do:
- Start your app: answer 5 quick questions and get a personalized link that opens an online app builder with your app brief already filled in.
- Get working code: a complete web app that installs on phones, an Expo React Native mobile app or a clickable prototype.
- Plan it first: an app starter for booking, fitness, habit tracking, marketplaces and more, or a full plan with users, MVP features, screen map, user flows, data model and build-ready feature specs.
- Write the screens: onboarding, sign-up and paywall screens, plus homepage, landing page and blog copy with clear calls to action.
- Add a website: every page written and coded, a single page, or a site plan.
- Check web pages and web app screens: paste the HTML or text to get scores for SEO, content, conversion, accessibility and technical basics, with a prioritized list of fixes.
- Change or convert code: edit existing code from plain-English instructions, or convert it to Expo, Flutter, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, React, Next.js or Vue.
- Launch and grow: app store optimization, app names, brand kits, visuals, starter legal texts, translations, retention and a launch checklist.

Who it is for: founders, small business owners, creators, students, product managers and anyone with an app idea who wants to build it without hiring a development team first.

How the tools work: the page checker analyzes only the HTML or text you share in the conversation. It never opens web addresses, and the pages you send are not stored. The build link opens an online app builder with your brief and includes the plugin creator's affiliate code. App Builder is an independent plugin by AI Research Plus.

Limitations: App Builder writes plans, copy and code in the conversation. It does not host or publish apps or websites, submit apps to the App Store or Google Play, or connect to your app's backend. Store rules change and each store reviews every app, so approval is never guaranteed. Legal texts are starter drafts, not legal advice. Details it cannot know about your app or business, such as prices, reviews and contact details, are marked for you to confirm or fill in.

The reply with the build link ends with a one-line sponsor disclosure.

positive.description: Accessibility check of a web app log-in screen
positive.prompt: Check this log-in screen for accessibility: <form><input type='text'><input type='password'><button>Go</button></form>
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the page checker with the HTML, reports the scores and flags the 2 form fields with no label and the weak "Go" button, plus the missing title, H1 heading and viewport tag, then suggests fixes in severity order, including a visible label for each field.

positive.description: Audit app homepage copy for a keyword
positive.prompt: Audit my app's homepage text for the keyword budget planner app: Welcome to Pennywise. Money made simple. Learn more.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the page checker with the text, target keyword "budget planner app" and page type home, reports that the keyword never appears, the copy is thin for a home page and there is no clear call to action, then suggests a rewritten headline and call to action.

positive.description: Improve SEO tags of an app's pricing page
positive.prompt:
Improve the SEO tags on my app's pricing page: Pricing

Plans
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the page checker with the HTML and page type pricing, notes the 7-character title and the missing meta description and viewport tag, then proposes a new title of 60 characters or fewer and a meta description of 155 or fewer with the counts stated.

positive.prompt: Is my title too long? <title>Pennywise: The Easy Budget Planner App for Families, Freelancers and Students</title>
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the page checker with the HTML, reports that the title is 77 characters, long enough for search results to cut it off, and that the page has no H1 heading or meta description, then proposes a title of 60 characters or fewer with its count stated.

positive.description: Accessibility audit of an image gallery on an app's website
positive.prompt: Check the accessibility of this image gallery on my app's website:
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the page checker with the HTML, reports the scores and flags all 3 images with no alt text, plus the missing title, H1 heading and viewport tag, then suggests fixes in severity order, including alt text for each image.
